items.summary: I have been playing with a lot of $20 devices with no keyboards or screens. I wanted to use speech to interact with them, but without it having to run through a cloud service or use a fixed command vocabulary. I worked with Claude to implement high performance 4bit int kernels for the ESP32S3 and P4 and quantize some larger STT and TTS models. Surprisingly, it's quite usable on these tiny boards. Also includes a finetuned model that can better cope with my diesel drones, hacking coughs, and mumbling. Works with Micropython (RAM scarcity issues) and AtomVM (better).

items.title: Show HN: I made a Jackbox-style tower defense game where trivia earns you gold
items.summary: My friends and I have always loved a party game to end the night. So, the day after I decided to quit my job, I started building a Jackbox-style game site just for us. The name... couchslop. As the name suggests, the idea behind couchslop is to create a playable game as fast as possible, then iterate on it until it's actually fun. The first game, Crystal Ridge Defense, is a multiplayer tower defense game where your team defends against waves of ships (psst, one person can play the villain and send ships at everyone else). Open it on whatever is plugged into your TV and everyone scans in to use

Show HN: I had 100 tabs open, so I built Daysift with AI powered by Proton
items.summary: I built Daysift because I kept ending up with 100+ tabs open just to avoid losing things I had seen or browsed before. Bookmarks never really worked for me because often you don't remember where something was, or what it was called. However, often I remembered what it was about. It's a Chrome extension that gives you a private way to find anything you visited before. It currently filters out noise, or things that don't associate with productivity or loosely with work. It's local first and designed around not retaining any data remotely. The AI layer is powered by Proton Lumo. It can also run A

items.summary: We just open sourced Chelis, a programming language we built focused on agent authorship and human supervision. You can find a longer intro on our site: https://chelis.ch/blog/launch/ But here are the key things a HN reader might like to know: * Statically typed, compiled, functional language, with heavy influences from ML family languages * Built for agent authorship of programs across the compiler, MCP, skills, and remdiation paths * Formal methods baked in via SMT and related solvers being connected with the type system in the compiler * Rich support for numerical programs and mathematicall
